kaigo-completeness-measurement-context.heading: Report time, site and circumstances alongside measurements
paragraphs: Vital signs are information indicating vital activity, such as temperature and pulse. Record values together with measurement time, site, device or method and known circumstances. Preserve values and units accurately without guessing missing conditions. The recipient needs to understand when and under what conditions each value was obtained.

Temperature may be measured at different sites or with different devices, such as under the arm, in the ear or at the forehead. Two readings from different sites or methods cannot be treated as a change measured under identical conditions. Preserve the original records and check each condition. However, differing conditions alone do not justify ignoring a higher value or the person feeling unwell.

Consider vital signs alongside the person’s own words, observations and differences from usual. A report of tiredness and measured values are both necessary information. One value not being high does not establish that overall health is without problems. Distinguish unchecked items from items with no abnormalities.

Breathing, pulse and blood pressure vary with activity, physical and mental condition and other factors. Measurement posture also matters for blood pressure. Recording known circumstances, such as immediately after activity, helps interpret change but does not establish cause. Do not conclude “because of activity” or “because of age”; communicate observed changes separately from unknowns.

Measure according to device instructions, confirmed individual support arrangements, facility procedures and your responsibilities. Forehead devices in particular require checking model-specific conditions. Do not derive independent fever criteria, repeat-measurement times or counts, or treatments from this lesson. Ask the responsible nursing staff or other appropriate person if unsure about methods or judgments.

Report concerning changes to the facility-designated recipient with measurement conditions, complaints, observations and unchecked items as well as values. In urgent situations, seek immediate assistance and follow facility emergency procedures rather than prioritizing a completed record. Known facts can be communicated before causes or diagnoses are established.

Learning scene: temperature was measured under the arm at 08:00. At 15:30, after the person returned from an activity, the forehead was measured with another device. The person says “I feel tired.” Separate both measurement conditions and communicate their words and the unchecked pulse and breathing. Do not conclude fever, cause or overall health from two values alone. Organize information to share the change with the person responsible.

176.title: Report time, site and circumstances alongside measurements
objectives: Explain conditions needed to understand measurements.
Report the person’s own words, observed facts and unchecked items separately.
176.context: Learn to communicate values with their circumstances through a scene comparing temperatures obtained under different conditions.
176.artCaption: A care worker talks with the person while recording. A blood-pressure cuff is visible on the arm.

weekly-kaigo-completeness-measurement-co.prompt: Which record and handover is appropriate for this scene?
options: Record activity as the cause of the higher 15:30 value and omit tiredness as unrelated to measurements.
Record the values as a change under identical conditions and diagnose fever solely from the increase.
Record each time, site and device, the recent activity, the person’s own words and unchecked pulse and breathing separately, and report the change to the responsible person.
Because conditions differ, postpone reporting the higher value and tiredness as unsuitable for comparison.
rationales: Recent activity is a fact, but it alone does not establish why the value rose. Report tiredness alongside measurements.
Sites and devices differ, so these are not readings under identical conditions. Do not determine fever from this information alone; communicate conditions and the person’s state.
Separating conditions, the person’s own words and unchecked items helps the recipient understand. Share concerns without determining a disease or cause from numbers alone.
Checking different conditions differs from not reporting change. Do not ignore the higher value or tiredness; communicate known information to the person responsible.
weekly-kaigo-completeness-measurement-co.reading: The 08:00 temperature record was measured under the arm. At 15:30, another care worker measured the forehead with a different device after the resident returned from an activity, recording only “the new value is higher.” The person says “I feel tired.” Pulse and breathing have not yet been checked.
